scores.tell: Clock is dead-frontal with a flat striped backdrop and no ground or depth layers. Real cards do this too (the towel), but the thick rim reads slightly swollen.
The hat is seen from a mild high angle with the brim ellipse. The radial-ray background is flat, with no ground plane and no foreground. Close to the real flat-backdrop cards.
The anchor is tilted in a flat view with no top face. The stripe backdrop is flat, so there is no depth layering. Rope wraps are plausible, but the form reads flat-on and a little stiff.
The clock has a slight turn, a visible rim thickness, a ground line, and a contact shadow. The depth layering matches the real cards. Only the stripes against the horizon band are slightly odd.

The glass is seen from a slightly high angle with an elliptical rim. The table edge and shadow give a consistent ground plane, and the background is a simple pattern. The straw and umbrella share the same view.
The seahorse is a flat side-on painted view with no ground or depth layers. The underwater gradient with light rays looks like a different, more painterly illustration style.

The ball sits on sand with a consistent ground plane, a mild camera height, and a soft contact shadow. The wavy dune background is simpler, in layers, and not heavily blurred. This matches the real cards.
The locker has a three-quarter view with a visible top face, a floor and wall, and a baseboard. Perspective is mild, though the open door and the interior shelves are a bit busy.
The clock is nearly the same as c119 with a slight turn and a ground band. The rim is a little flat and frontal, with a weak contact shadow.
The anchor is tilted in a flat view with a diagonal stripe backdrop and no ground. The pose is flat and frontal, close to the real towel and saddle cards. The rope wraps give some depth.
